content.intro: Generic Constraints is lesson 97 in Generics and Type-Safe Reuse. Generics let one implementation work with multiple types while preserving compile-time type information. Constraints state which capabilities the implementation requires.
content.why_it_matters: Generics avoid duplicating algorithms while preserving useful information about the values being processed. This lesson focuses on generic constraints and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Generics let one implementation work with multiple types while preserving compile-time type information. Constraints state which capabilities the implementation requires.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to learn it
content_blocks.text: Start with the smallest valid case for generic constraints. Predict the output, run or inspect the example in the stated toolchain, then change one input or rule and compare the result. For production code, record assumptions and verify boundary cases.

items.title: The where clause
items.text: Generics preserve type information while letting one implementation work with many types. Constraints state requirements at compile time; variance changes assignment compatibility only in supported input/output positions.

items.title: Reference-type constraints
items.text: A generic constraint states the operations or type relationships the implementation is allowed to rely on.

items.title: Value-type constraints
items.text: A generic constraint states the operations or type relationships the implementation is allowed to rely on.

items.title: Constructor constraints
items.text: Make required state explicit during object creation and keep partially initialized objects from escaping.

items.title: Interface constraints
items.text: An interface describes a capability callers can depend on without depending on the implementation details.

items.title: Base-class constraints
items.text: A generic constraint states the operations or type relationships the implementation is allowed to rely on.

items.title: Nullable and unmanaged constraints
items.text: Treat absence explicitly. Check null before dereferencing, use a deliberate fallback, and do not silence nullable warnings without evidence.

content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.
